solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Extremist in bizarre rituals is thrown out

indicators.note: something bizarre is twisted out of its normal shape, so the remaining letters are rearranged
what is thrown out is removed, so those letters leave the word they sit in

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, the letters to be removed

explanation.surface: A fanatic within some strange ceremonial group gets expelled.
explanation.walkthrough: Take IS out of RITUALS, leaving RTUAL, and rearrange to ULTRA.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultra is a person holding extreme views, a straightforward noun synonym for a zealot.

clue.text: Clapped-out like a brolly

blocks.note: first meaning: worn out, exhausted
second meaning, read as two words: an umbrella in use is raised over the head

explanation.walkthrough: A brolly is an umbrella; when it is being used, it is up. The phrase splits into 'used' plus 'up' for the second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapped-out is British slang for worn out and exhausted, the ordinary meaning of the phrase as one idiom.

clue.text: Seasons in the case of Blackpool: rainy or windy!

indicators.note: to season is to mix flavourings through a dish, so the letters are blended into a new order
the case of something is its outside, so only the first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the outside letters of the resort's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gloomy weather report on Blackpool, the English seaside resort: every season is either wet or blustery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Windy' looks like weather, but it is the definition, read as winding (rhymes with finding); 'Seasons' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Windy here means winding and twisting, and a labyrinthine path turns and coils like a maze.

clue.text: Highland forecaster upset by cuts

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: a spaer is a Scottish word for a fortune-teller, one who spaes or foretells

explanation.surface: A Scottish weather forecaster is upset by job losses.
explanation.walkthrough: Highland signals a Scots word; to spae is to prophesy, so a spaer foretells the future rather than the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: To reap is to cut a crop such as corn, so the verb form matches the third-person cuts.

clue.text: Article about large Mediterranean units

blocks.note: ART is the dictionary abbreviation for article
A is an abbreviation for about, as in dates
L is the standard clothing abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A piece of writing about large units in the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: ARTAL is a plural of rotl, a weight once used in Mediterranean and Middle Eastern countries.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotl is a traditional measure of weight in the Levant and North Africa; artal is one of its plurals.

clue.text: Pleased to keep one favoured cereal ingredient

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: glad means pleased
the Roman numeral for one
to be in is to be in favour or fashionable

explanation.surface: Someone is happy to keep a single favoured breakfast cereal component.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Favoured' looks like a description of the cereal, but it is wordplay; the definition is the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Gliadin is a protein found in wheat and other cereal grains, part of gluten.

clue.text: Record gambling game in cabin

blocks.note: a log is a written record, as a ship's log
house, or housey-housey, is an old name for bingo, played for money

explanation.surface: Someone notes down a game of chance played inside a hut.
explanation.walkthrough: House (housey-housey) is a British name for bingo, the numbers game with a caller.
explanation.definitionFit: A log house is a cabin built of timber logs, the kind of simple dwelling a frontier settler builds.

clue.text: Insectivore not popular in a south-eastern state

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other, which surrounds it

blocks.note: taken as written
GA is the postal abbreviation for Georgia, a state in the south-east of the USA
out is the opposite of in, unfashionable

explanation.surface: Some insect-eating creature has fallen out of favour in a south-eastern American state.
explanation.walkthrough: A and GA together surround OUT: A G(OUT)A.
explanation.definitionFit: The agouta is the Haitian solenodon, a small shrew-like mammal that feeds on insects.

clue.text: Short written treatise on area not special for examiner

indicators.note: not tells us that what follows is missing from the word

blocks.note: DISS is the short form of dissertation, a written treatise
a sector is an area or zone
S is the abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: A brief dissertation on some field, unremarkable, put forward for an examiner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not special' works only on the area word, dropping its abbreviation for special.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissector cuts up and studies a body or specimen in detail, so is a close examiner of it.

clue.text: Is the outline styled as such?

definitions.text: Is the outline styled as such?

indicators.note: to style something is to shape it afresh, so the preceding letters take on a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written, twelve letters

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a drawing's outline has been done in a particular manner.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a shape drawn only by its outline is shown in silhouette.
explanation.definitionFit: A silhouette is a dark shape showing only an outline, so something styled that way is shown by its outline alone.

clue.text: Head, one ending in the soup

blocks.note: first meaning: informal word for the head or brain
second meaning: a strip of pasta, one of many that finish up in a bowl of soup

explanation.walkthrough: 'In the soup' suggests being in trouble, but here it is literal: pasta strips really do end up in soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodle is slang for the head, and a noodle is also a strip of pasta served in broth.

clue.text: Your setter finally tails off? The reverse, lots on offer here

indicators.note: with its tail off, each word loses its final letter
the reverse instructs us to read the result backwards

blocks.note: Tim Moorey, one of the setters of the Mephisto puzzle, so 'your setter' is the person addressing the solver
last means finally, in the end

explanation.surface: A self-deprecating setter wonders whether he is finally fading, then reverses himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Both MOOREY and LAST lose their tails to give MOORE and LAS; the whole is then read backwards. This works only knowing that Tim Moorey set this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A saleroom is an auction house, where lots, items for sale, are offered to bidders.

clue.text: Matrix ducks accommodating extreme Brazilian state

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room to, so one piece is housed inside another

blocks.note: mat is a printing term for a matrix, the mould type is cast in
a duck is a score of zero in cricket, and zero looks like O
gross means flagrant or extreme

explanation.surface: A grid of waterfowl houses some outlandish feature of Brazil.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a batter's score of nothing in cricket, hence a pair of Os.
explanation.definitionFit: Mato Grosso is one of the large inland states of western Brazil, a proper name given by category.

clue.text: Dislike days without a course of action ending in victory

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the following letter is removed
the ending of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the letter to be removed
a path is a course or way of acting
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone resents days that lack a plan leading to a win.
explanation.walkthrough: DAYS drops its A to leave DYS, a prefix-like start meaning bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyspathy is an old word for antipathy or lack of sympathy, so a feeling of aversion.

clue.text: Film unhappy defeat

blocks.note: to shoot a scene is to film it
feeling down is feeling sad

explanation.surface: A gloomy film about a sad loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' and 'unhappy' look like a noun and adjective; both are wordplay, and the definition is at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoot down an argument or proposal is to defeat it decisively, an idiomatic verb phrase.

clue.text: University in turn mocks sexual disease? Supposedly

blocks.note: your go is your turn in a game
U is the abbreviation for university
to jeer is to mock

explanation.surface: A university, in its turn, ridicules a supposed venereal infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'University in turn' is read loosely: U takes its place next after the word for turn. The word comes from Shakespeare and its meaning is uncertain, hence 'Supposedly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Goujeers appears in Shakespeare's King Lear and is traditionally glossed as venereal disease, though the sense is doubtful.

clue.text: Sheep shelter from sun on hill

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for sun
a tell is an ancient mound or hill built up from settlement remains

explanation.surface: A sheep finds shade from the sun on a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sits after the sun: S is followed by TELL. A tell is an archaeologist's word for a mound in the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: A stell is a Scottish and northern word for an enclosure or walled shelter for sheep.

clue.text: Very good old van for youngster or banger from the Gorbals?

indicators.note: the van is the front of an army, so only the leading letter is taken

blocks.note: pi is short for pious, very good
O is the abbreviation for old
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A good old delivery van for a young lad, or a battered car from a Glasgow slum.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gorbals is a district of Glasgow, so a Scots word is wanted; banger is a firework, not an old car.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioy is a Scottish homemade firework, a cone of damp gunpowder; a banger is a firework that explodes.

clue.text: Two notes on long, decorative braid

blocks.note: so (soh) and ut (an old name for doh) are notes of the sol-fa scale
to ache for is to long for

explanation.surface: A couple of musical notes are written on a long, ornate trim.
explanation.walkthrough: UT is the old name for the first note of the scale, now doh.
explanation.definitionFit: Soutache is a narrow flat braid used to trim and ornament clothing.

clue.text: Seattle plant succeeded with present and former President

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees
now is the present time
either George Bush, both former US presidents

explanation.surface: A factory in Seattle prospered under the present and a previous US president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a factory, Seattle being home to Boeing; it is a shrub of the American north-west.
explanation.definitionFit: Snowbush is a ceanothus shrub with white flowers native to western North America, including Washington State.

clue.text: Quite filling spread with pasty

indicators.note: filling means occupying the inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: to sow seed is to spread or scatter it
all means quite or completely, as in all alone

explanation.surface: Quite a filling spread served with a pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pasty' looks like a Cornish pie, a noun; it is the adjective meaning pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Sallow describes a sickly yellowish complexion, and a pasty face is similarly pale and unhealthy.

clue.text: Rod reportedly became pale

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so a word is chosen for how it sounds

blocks.note: a wand is a slender rod, pronounced like the past tense of wan

explanation.surface: A fisherman's rod is said to have lost its colour.
explanation.definitionFit: To wan is an old verb meaning to grow pale, and its past tense matches became pale.

clue.text: Flies back for boring thing in Scotland

indicators.note: back means the word is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: bots are botflies, whose larvae live in animals

explanation.surface: Insects heading home for something dull in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' looks like dull, but means drilling holes.
explanation.definitionFit: Stob is a Scots word for a bradawl, a small tool that bores holes, hence a boring tool.

clue.text: Outlaws second-class guys seeking publicity

indicators.note: seeking means going after, so one element is placed behind the other

blocks.note: B is the grade for second class
an ad, an advertisement, is publicity
guys are men

explanation.surface: Criminals and inferior men hungry for media attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Badmen are villains or outlaws, especially in Western films.

clue.text: Perfume ingredient: get it in Middle Eastern state, no question

indicators.note: no question means the abbreviation for question is removed
in places one piece inside the other, which surrounds it

blocks.note: read as the letter the solver is to get in, apparently T as in 'to a T'
Qatar is a Gulf state
Q is the abbreviation for question

explanation.surface: A perfumer is told to find a component in a Gulf state, no questions asked.
explanation.walkthrough: QATAR without Q is ATAR, and T goes inside. How 'get it' gives T is unclear to us; the rest of the parse is certain.
explanation.definitionFit: Attar is an essential oil distilled from flowers, especially rose petals, used as a base for perfume.

clue.text: Irishman who's learned nothing lost office

blocks.note: O looks like zero, nothing
L is the abbreviation for lost in league tables
the offices is an old euphemism for the lavatory

explanation.surface: An educated Irishman has nothing, having been turned out of his post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Office' looks like a job; it is the old euphemism for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: An ollav was a learned man or master poet in ancient Ireland, so the definition describes him exactly.

clue.text: Honour given to lecturer, one showing marks on script

blocks.note: the OBE is a British honour, Order of the British Empire
L is the abbreviation for lecturer
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lecturer receives an award, one marking exam scripts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one showing marks on script' suggests an examiner, but one is just I.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeli are dagger or division-sign symbols used in old texts to mark doubtful passages or footnotes.

clue.text: Spring roll said to be refined

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word is chosen for its sound

blocks.note: a well is a spring of water
a roll is a small loaf of bread

explanation.surface: A springtime bread roll is said to be quite sophisticated.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well-bred has good manners from a polite upbringing, so is cultivated and refined.

clue.text: Heraldic animals formerly seen in French city square

indicators.note: seen in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: Lille is a city in northern France
once means formerly
S is the abbreviation for square

explanation.surface: Heraldic beasts formerly displayed in the square of a French town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Formerly' looks like a time marker for the surface, but it supplies the inserted word.
explanation.definitionFit: A lioncel or lioncelle is a small lion borne in heraldry, often several on one shield.

clue.text: Weapon's protective covering whitish as mentioned

indicators.note: as mentioned means spoken out, so the words are chosen for their sound

blocks.note: armour is protective covering, said in a non-rhotic British accent
a light colour is pale and close to white

explanation.surface: A gun has a pale protective casing.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech, without a sounded R, armour ends in the same vowel as the start of the brand name.
explanation.definitionFit: The ArmaLite is an American assault rifle, a brand name for a lightweight firearm.

clue.text: Wyn, once a gorgeous lady is Sorbian

blocks.note: wyn or wen is an Old English runic letter, no longer used
a dish is slang for an attractive person

explanation.surface: Wyn was once a stunning woman of Sorbian descent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wyn' looks like a Welsh name, but it is the old letter also spelt wen.
explanation.definitionFit: Wendish is another name for Sorbian, the Slavic language of the Wends in eastern Germany.

clue.text: Fox TV's latest: 9/11 vacuously presented

indicators.note: the latest is the most recent, so the final letter is taken
vacuously means emptied, so only the outer letters remain

blocks.note: the final letter of the abbreviation
IX is the Roman numeral for nine
eleven written out, with only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Fox News's latest: a hollow presentation of the September 11 attacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fox' looks like the news channel, but it is the definition; 9/11 is two separate numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: A vixen is a female fox, a specific example of the animal named by the definition.
